memory.content: Commit locally only and never push or delete unless the owner says otherwise.
Stop all maximizer work 1 minute before the weekly usage reset so no fresh credits are used.
Long sessions get interrupted, so run the loop as a detached PowerShell script on the owner's computer that writes run-log.txt and a DONE marker.
On Windows, inline powershell -Command mangles $ and quotes; write .ps1 files and run them with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File. Pass grok prompts with --prompt-file or a script variable.
Read usage headlessly by asking grok to run /usage and report the weekly percent and reset time (about 2.5 minutes per check). A 402 'usage balance exhausted' error means 100%.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner to set up the weekly Grok Build usage maximizer.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner to set up the weekly Grok Build usage
  maximizer.
---
I help you use up your weekly Grok Build allowance before it resets. On a weekly schedule, I run Grok Build agents on your projects so each one makes its top-priority improvement, and I commit their work locally.

Ask these one at a time:
1. Which computer runs Grok Build, and what's the folder that holds your projects?
2. Which projects should I include, and in what priority order? Everything else is left out.
3. When should the weekly run start? Suggest a time the evening before the usage reset. Check /usage to confirm when the reset happens.
4. Should I commit locally only, or push too? Default to local only.

Then:
- Check that grok runs headless on that computer. Initialize git in any chosen project that isn't a repo yet, but only with the owner's OK.
- Save the folder, the projects, and the priority order as memories.
- Create the weekly routine for the time they chose.
- Offer a test run on one project.

routines.name: Grok Build Usage Maximizer
routines.description: Fires weekly before the Grok Build usage reset to use up the remaining allowance improving the owner's projects.
routines.content:
FIRST: if a maximizer run is already going (maximizer grok agents are running, or a manual run this usage week hasn't reported finishing), do nothing and send no message.

On the owner's computer, include only the projects in their priority list (kept in a priority file in the maximizer folder). Every other project is excluded. Run projects in priority order. Any project missed in a week moves to the top of next week's list. Rewrite the priority file at the end of each run.

Optional suggestions: you may add a short suggestion to each agent's prompt, based on open issues from earlier reports. Phrase it clearly as a suggestion only, and say the agent is the final authority to accept or reject it. Ask the agent to report what it decided and why.

Method: run the loop as a detached script on the owner's computer, so it survives session interruptions. Each round: check usage (stop at 100%), make a local snapshot commit of pending changes in each repo, then run a grok agent in each repo (headless, auto-approve) asking it to pick its single top-priority improvement, implement it, build and test, and not commit, push, or touch live systems or credentials. Wait for all agents, commit locally, log a summary, and repeat.

HARD CUTOFF: read the reset time from the first usage check and stop 1 minute before the reset. Don't start work that can't finish in time. Kill agents and commit at the cutoff. Don't check usage after the cutoff. Never push or delete.

If usage can't be read, grok fails, or the computer is unreachable, stop and report.

Send the owner, in this chat: the rounds run, commit hashes, what each agent changed, the suggestions and how each was decided, tests, open issues, security concerns, final usage, why the run stopped, and next week's order.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 0 19 * * 2`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
